title: Who played in the Virginia's band
summary: Howard names Arthur Twine on piano and Ted Brinson on bass in a five-piece band that played dancing; he also sang.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You mentioned the piano player. You said Charles Lawrence was the second piano player now who played first, in the beginning?
Who played the piano in the beginning?
When you first --
It was -- let me see, wait a minute. Let me start at the bass player, will you?
Okay.
Harvey Brooks.
Harvey Brooks was the piano player. You said the bass player was Ted Brinson.
Ted Brinson, yeah. Then later come --
The second pianist was Charles Lawrence, but you said there was another piano player when you started the job.
What was his name? He was a young kid.
Arthur Twine?
Arthur Twine, that was the piano player. He got too --
What happened, he stayed for a while and then he had to leave?
No, he had to leave -- he stayed there with me.
I thought you said Charles was the
second piano player, Charles Lawrence.
No.
So Twine stayed all the time.
Twine played with me all the time.
For 14 years.
Almost 14 years. He -- and then I took in -- who was it? Who else was a piano player? I don't remember. I can't remember.
So was it dancing there, did you have to play for dancing?
Yeah, played for dancing.
Dancing.
Uh-huh.
Mostly dancing. In other words, you had a trio or --
I had five people.
You had five people at Virginia's? So you had a trumpet?
No, I didn't have a trumpet, did I?
Okay. You had a piano, Arthur Twine.
Yeah.
You had a bass player, Ted Brinson. Do you remember who your drummer was?
The drummer?
(inaudible) Susie might know too.
I can't think of who the drummer was. Boy, I'm telling you, this takes the run out of me, because I can't remember all of them.
That's all right. You know, it's okay. Well, it'll come to you, probably the moment we relax a minute you'll think of the drummer.
Yeah, It'll come to me.
Anyway, we're getting most of them, but you think you had five pieces, more than four?
I had five pieces.
Were you doing any singing at that point at Virginia's?
Yeah, I did a lot of singing. Oh I aint going to tell you all them things. Ms. Willard: Why not?
You did, huh? You want to keep secrets from us. See, we know about some of these things.
I couldn't sing that well.
But they liked what you were doing. You had certain special material to sing.
Yes, they did. They did. They liked what I was doing.
That's why they kept you there. They liked you.
Just kept me there all that time. The longest time I was there.
